newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight inquiry steady but fixtures scarce.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight inquiry steady but fixtures scarce.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a rush of new business on Tuesday but fixtures were relatively thin on the ground, shipbrokers said.
Despite a nationwide 24-hour port strike in Brazil, called by the National Portworker's Federation, demand for Brazilian sugar cargoes remained steady, they said.

E D & F Man was active on the market on Tuesday, quoting for 14,000 tonnes min/max bulk sugar from Maceio or Recife to Durban or Beira for 10 days notice. It was also said to have fixed last week's order for 4,500 tonnes in bags from Motril to Mersin.
The only other firmer business came from Andre which fixed 5,000 tonnes in bags Rouen to Nouakchott for early December.
Czarnikow Rionda quoted for 12,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Chile for January 1/10.
CSR was also in the market with a new order, quoting for 15,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to south China for prompt/10 days notice.

CSR was also in the market for 16,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Japan for December 15/25. Market sources said the charterer had tonnage booked at $19, down from the $21 reported for CSR's last such similar fixture.

Genoc was open for 23,500/24,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Salaverry to U.S. Gulf/Atlantic for December 17/24 and shipbrokers said its prompt bagged order for 13/14,000 tonnes from Poland to Algeria with options of Egypt and Red Sea was still open.
Louis Dreyfus quoted for 14,300 tonnes min/max bulk sugar from Rostock to Tunisia for prompt dates.
